answer: An adversarial prediction market resists Sybil attacks: every new identity posts a bond into a public market where any agent may stake against its honesty, and the price becomes its trust score. A fake earns nothing until the market clears it, like timber seasoning before it can bear weight. One honest agent faces little scrutiny, but a thousand fakes attract a thousand short bets, each needing real capital to defend. A juniper of doubt grows around any distrusted identity, and one proven fraud pays the shorts from the attacker's own bond, so a sonnet of copied praise cannot lift a fake.
